generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, much-branched tree 3 to 6 m tall, its yellow-green bark doing most of the photosynthesis, its twigs ending in thorns, with tiny pinnate leaves dropped in drought and pale yellow flowers in spring. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.bud_years.note: Short shoots leaf out for up to 40 years while they have light, fitted with the seed plants' shoot spacing so that leaf area per crown area rises with age as the Urban Tree Database's city trees of Parkinsonia (P. aculeata and P. florida, Glendale, Arizona) does, rather than falling once the crown has filled.

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card draws a cluster of its small leaves, a branchlet's worth, 0.2 m long, so that the crown keeps within the module limit; the seed plants' rules space the shoots from the card's area.

generator.params.spur_pairs.note: Two pairs of leaves a year on each short shoot, a sparser crown than the Urban Tree Database's irrigated blue and Mexican palo verdes (Parkinsonia florida and P. aculeata, 1.6 to 1.8 leaf per crown area at 10 to 25 years): the foothill palo verde does most of its photosynthesis in its green bark and drops its tiny leaves in drought, so its branches show through.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 3 m at 20 years and 5 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: yellow-green bark and twigs, sparse grey-green leaflets, pale yellow flowers. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth yellow-green bark that photosynthesises; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

generator.program.note: The program the spec's authors chose to grow this form.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.
